tagline: Orbiter of India's second Moon mission, still mapping the Moon with eight instruments after Vikram's loss in 2019
description: The orbiter of Chandrayaan-2, India's first attempt at a soft landing on the Moon. Launched on 2019-07-22 from Sriharikota on an LVM3 (then called GSLV Mk III) with the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover, the 2379 kg orbiter raised its own orbit around the Earth, was captured into lunar orbit on 2019-08-20 and released Vikram on 2019-09-02. Vikram crashed during its descent on 2019-09-06; the orbiter carries on in a polar orbit. Its eight instruments are the CLASS X-ray spectrometer, the XSM solar X-ray monitor, the DFSAR dual-frequency radar, the IIRS imaging infrared spectrometer, the ChACE-2 mass spectrometer, the TMC-2 terrain mapping camera, the RAMBHA-DFRS radio occultation experiment and the OHRC, a high-resolution camera that later imaged the Chandrayaan-3 landing site.
best_known_for: Orbiter of India's second Moon mission, still mapping the Moon with eight instruments after Vikram's loss in 2019
